reason: The DNA building blocks match positions beside existing DNA, suggesting the cell can use them to copy its instructions.
expectation: The cell will use the building blocks to make a copy of its DNA.

alternatives.reason: The fats might also help make extra membrane, which is the other goal.

effect: The cell now has copied DNA, so I can work on making extra membrane.
reaction: The picture makes it clearer that each chromosome has a copied partner.
reason: Membrane fats are the visible material for the remaining goal of making extra membrane.
expectation: The fats will add membrane to the growing cell.

effect: The new membrane is prepared in sacs but has not yet joined the cell boundary; the remaining goal is division.
reaction: I hadn't expected the membrane to be prepared separately before joining the boundary.
reason: The prepared membrane needs to join the cell, and the copied DNA is already inside it.
expectation: The new membrane will help the cell grow or divide, with a DNA copy going to each daughter cell.

effect: The membrane joined the boundary, and the copied chromosomes separated into two cells with complete matching sets. Further divisions produced a cell population.
reaction: The three-panel sequence made the connection between growth, chromosome separation and division clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the membrane supply with the cell was most worthwhile because it showed how the prepared membrane and copied DNA contributed to division.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the membrane supply was a little less satisfying on its own because it prepared material without yet enlarging the cell.

surprise.text: I expected the fats to enlarge the cell directly, but they first formed membrane held in small sacs.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the goals and pictures gave each pairing a purpose, although the membrane-making structures themselves weren't explained in detail.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see what happens to the cell population, though this short chapter was mostly straightforward preparation followed by division.
